- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 10-15% above peak for next 5 days.
- If 3+ consecutive days of sentiment = 0.33 or 0.67, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging last 5 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– spikes (e.g., +0.67, -0.67, +0.67), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment decay factor (e.g., 0.85) to dampen forecast.
